source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use aspirin routinely for viral fever because Reye syndrome is associated with bacterial infections rather than viral illness.","B":"Delay aspirin until the viral fever has lasted at least 24 hours because duration of fever determines whether Reye syndrome can occur.","C":"Combine aspirin with acetaminophen during viral illness because concurrent acetaminophen prevents the aspirin-associated Reye risk.","D":"Avoid aspirin during a child or teenager’s viral illness unless a clinician specifically directs its use because of the Reye-syndrome association."}}
source_row.rationale: Aspirin labeling warns that children and teenagers who have or are recovering from chickenpox or flu-like symptoms should not use aspirin because of the association with Reye syndrome unless directed by a clinician.
